$comment: Shared behavioral contract for the dictionary correction pass.
The macOS app implements this logic in Swift.
Independent implementations drift. This file keeps every implementation honest:
each one must produce exactly the stated output for every case below.
1. Whole matches only  - a rule must never bite into a longer word.
2. Case-insensitive    - the trigger matches in any case; output is verbatim.
3. Longest match first - a longer trigger wins over a shorter overlapping one.
4. Glued words match   - parts may be separated by spaces or hyphens, including none.
5. Disabled is inert   - a disabled entry changes nothing.

cases.name: basic phrase replacement
cases.input: I write morning pages every day.
cases.expected: I write Morning Pages every day.

cases.name: glued together with no separator
cases.expected: I write Morning Pages every day.

cases.name: joined by a hyphen
cases.expected: I write Morning Pages every day.

cases.name: multiple spaces between parts
cases.input: I write morning  pages every day.
cases.expected: I write Morning Pages every day.

cases.name: must not corrupt a longer word that starts the same way
cases.input: Morningstar is bright and morningpagesx is not a phrase.
cases.expected: Morningstar is bright and morningpagesx is not a phrase.

cases.name: must not touch either ordinary word alone
cases.input: The morning is clear and the pages are ready.
cases.expected: The morning is clear and the pages are ready.

cases.name: longest trigger wins over a shorter overlapping one
counts repeated hits
cases.input: mornin pages, then mornin pages again, and mornin pages.
cases.expected: Morning Pages, then Morning Pages again, and Morning Pages.

cases.name: a disabled entry changes nothing
cases.input: I write morning pages every day.
cases.expected: I write morning pages every day.

cases.name: a term entry never rewrites text
single word trigger is honored when asked for
several independent rules in one pass
replacement containing regex metacharacters is literal
accented trigger matches decomposed input
cases.$comment: The input is deliberately NFD to cover macOS text normalization.
